properties.name: Palermo Chico
properties.source: GCBA, dataset "Áreas de Protección Histórica" (data.buenosaires.gob.ar/dataset/areas-proteccion-historica), APH3 "Ámbito Gran Bourg y Palermo Chico" (Ley 536/2000, vigente en el Código Urbanístico, Ley 6099)
properties.methodology: Convex hull of the 442 cataloged parcels tagged APH3 in the official per-parcel GeoJSON. This is a derived approximation of the legally protected area, not the exact polygon from the Código Urbanístico's plan annex (published only as a PDF plan, not open geodata).

properties.name: Belgrano R
properties.source: GCBA, dataset "Áreas de Protección Histórica", APH4 "Entorno Estación Belgrano R"
properties.methodology: Convex hull of the 50 cataloged parcels tagged APH4 in the official per-parcel GeoJSON. Same caveat as Palermo Chico: a derived approximation, not the exact legal polygon. Note this APH covers only the area immediately around Belgrano R train station, which is smaller than the colloquial real-estate "Belgrano R" neighborhood.

properties.name: Palermo Soho
properties.source: Billiken ("¿Sabías que hay diecinueve sub-barrios no oficiales dentro de Palermo?", billiken.lat): "queda al sur de la Avenida Juan B. Justo"; cross-checked against Mudafy.com.ar, which bounds it by Av. Scalabrini Ortiz, Av. Córdoba, Av. Juan B. Justo and Av. Santa Fe.
properties.methodology: No official boundary exists for this name. Polygon built by pulling the real OpenStreetMap line geometry of each boundary street named by the source, keeping only the points within ~1-1.4km of this sub-barrio's own listings' centroid (or a manual estimate where no listings exist yet), and taking the convex hull of the pooled points. This hugs the named streets without depending on exact street-to-street intersections (most of these avenues don't literally cross near the area, or OSM splits them into many short way segments).
